speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) whether the Ministry is considering a review of the Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act to explicitly prohibit greenwashing by businesses operating in Singapore; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider funding community education programmes to raise awareness among consumers about greenwashing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These can be found on both the CCCS website as well as the CASE website.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: My question really is on, how do we align this with our Singapore Green Plan?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In terms of legislation, we are looking at businesses being a bit more ethical in their practices and being aligned with our Green Plan as well, but at the same time, they are also trying to make a living.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: So, that is one question – how are we going to get the legislation to move into being aligned the Green Plan?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The next question is, when we are advising our consumers, are they aware of the implication of this?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Because a lot of the terms that are being used is very vague.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: So, I think in trying to get our population to be aligned with some of the initiatives that we are trying to do in terms of sustainability, it is important that we consider how we educate our consumers.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In fact, indeed, these are all part of an overarching move for us within the Singapore Green Plan, to make both consumers as well as businesses understand.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And as both consumers demand more of green supply chains and value chains, upstream as well as downstream, so too businesses have that understanding of consumer preferences as well.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If I can also supplement the answer to the Member's question, about both what we are trying to do upstream, in terms of consumer education, which the Assoc Prof had mentioned earlier on, as well as downstream.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If you are a consumer, or if you are a business, how can you take concrete action?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: On the upstream, we have these consumer education tips that I mentioned, both by CCCS as well as CASE.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I have just checked it out this morning.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I think we can do a lot better.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, if Assoc Prof Razwana, other Members of this House and other members in the community can give us even more tips to enhance that, we would welcome those suggestions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, if you were a consumer and you encounter what you think would be greenwashing claims made by businesses on your purchases, please do approach CASE for assistance.
